passage:
Coach's note, college hockey squad, for my own records.
Swati, our right half, showed me her phone today. She has been tracking her cycle alongside her training log for months and has noticed that a few days each month she feels heavier, teary and slower off the mark, while the following week she feels unstoppable. She was worried I would see it as weakness. I told her it is the opposite: it is information about her own body. We agreed that on her low-energy days she will do skills drills and lighter conditioning, and push hard on her strong days. She will tell me with one word, "green" or "amber", so she needn't explain in front of the team. I will check in next month on how it is working.
Suraj

qa.a: "Green" or "amber".

qa.q: What was Swati worried about when she showed the coach her phone?
qa.a: She was anxious that Suraj would see her low days as weakness.

qa.q: Why is the plan a wise one?
qa.a: It uses Swati's own pattern to plan lighter drills on low days and hard training on strong days, without treating her as weak.

qa.q: How does Suraj see Swati's tracking?
qa.a: Suraj sees it as useful information about her own body, not a weakness, and adjusts training to match.

grounding: Shows a young woman tracking her cycle, spotting lower-energy and stronger days, and planning lighter work without treating it as weakness.

passage:
Tuesday night
Cried at a dog food advert today. Actually cried. Then snapped at Dilnaz for leaving her mug on my desk, and felt awful. When I opened my cycle tracker to log it, there it was again: the same few days every month when I'm low, teary and everything feels too loud. A week later I'm the girl who volunteers for every presentation. Seeing the pattern on the screen made me feel less crazy. It isn't weakness; it's just my rhythm. So next month I'm not booking the debate trials on those days. Early nights, lighter reading, a long walk. I told Dilnaz and said sorry about the mug. She said she's noticed her own low days too, and we're going to compare notes. Weirdly comforting.
Mahima

qa.q: What made Mahima cry today?
qa.a: A dog food advert.

qa.q: How did Mahima feel after seeing the pattern in the tracker?
qa.a: She felt relieved and less crazy, seeing it as her rhythm rather than weakness.

qa.q: How does Mahima plan to use what she learned?
qa.a: By not booking debate trials on the low days and planning early nights, lighter reading and a walk instead.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz feel about Mahima's apology and explanation?
qa.a: She seems understanding and even glad, since she has noticed her own low days and wants to compare notes.

grounding: Illustrates a young woman noticing through tracking that some days bring tearfulness and low energy, and planning rest without seeing it as weakness.

passage: In the tailoring shop she ran from the front room of the family house in Bhilwara, Kashish kept a small calendar behind the sewing machine, marked with tiny red dots only she understood. For six months she had noted her cycle and, beside it, how she felt: tired, weepy, strong, fast. The pattern surprised her. A few days each month she snapped at customers and cried over a crooked seam; other weeks she could stitch three blouses before lunch. Wedding season was coming. Instead of promising everything to everyone, she put the big lehenga orders in her strong weeks and kept the low days for hemming and buttons. When Shreya, her younger sister, teased her about the calendar, Kashish just said, "It's not weakness. It's planning." Shreya thought about that, then borrowed a pen.

qa.a: Behind the sewing machine.

passage: In their tiny dorm room in Seoul, Yara stuck a paper chart to the wardrobe door: a row of dates, each with a coloured dot for how she felt. After three months, Soo-ah, her roommate, saw it too: the blue dots, for tearful and flat, came in the same few days before Yara's period; the gold ones, for energetic, came about a week after. "You had your big exam in a blue week last term," Soo-ah said. Yara groaned, remembering crying in the library over a missing highlighter. This term she booked her swim time-trial for a gold week and marked the blue days for gentle walks, early nights and easy reading. When the blue days came, she still felt low. But she didn't call herself lazy. She made tea, pulled on thick socks, and let herself rest.

qa.q: What colour were the tearful, flat days on the chart?
qa.a: Blue.

qa.q: How did Yara feel on the blue days this term?
qa.a: She still felt low, but calmer and kinder to herself, no longer calling herself lazy.

qa.q: What did Yara change this term?
qa.a: She booked her swim time-trial for a gold week and planned gentle walks, early nights and easy reading for the blue days.

qa.q: How does Soo-ah help?
qa.a: Soo-ah spots the pattern and gently points out last term's timing, supporting Yara without judging.

grounding: Shows a young woman charting her cycle, recognising tearful and energetic phases, and planning rest without treating it as weakness.

passage: In the university biology lab, Deepika kept a small notebook next to her pipettes. Kiran, her lab partner, finally asked what she was always jotting down. 'My cycle and my moods,' Deepika said, unembarrassed. 'Three months of notes. See? Around these days I'm tired and tear up at nothing. Around these, I'm sharp and can manage long runs.' She had moved the fiddly cell counts to her strong week and kept the low days for reading papers and leaving on time. 'I used to think I was just weak on those days,' she said. 'Now it's just planning.' Kiran looked at the neat columns. 'That's smarter than my to-do list.'
